m4.title: Wire the contract into COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json -- asymmetrically
m4.imperative: verify-orientation becomes a command postcondition c2 on the CONTEXT step; verify-frame becomes a command postcondition on the PLAN step. verify-frame must NOT run at context -- no frame exists there, and making an absent frame pass at context would destroy m2's ABSENT-frame refusal. Record that reasoning in the imperative PROSE so a future implementer sees the road not to take. Use <repo-root>, never a relative path (#341 is out of scope). Give the plan check override_policy {allowed:true, authority:human, reason_required:true} so a trivial-change escape is a recorded waiver; keep the context check tighter (no policy). Keep gate-vs-report flag-flippable. Name the frame path the plan step must write so the check is satisfiable.

why_trail.why: handoff complete: task, protected intent, deliverables, allowed scope, exclusions, constraints, required evidence, stop conditions, return format all present. g1 artifacts read: map_orient.py (orient + verify-orientation, frozen exit codes 0/10/11/12/13, reserved stdout literals), its floor, the mutation harness, and the spine template's context/plan tasks.

Anchor change landed: tasks.context.imperative now anchors the map read to 'Before you open any source file', names map_orient.py orient with --root <repo-root> --work-id <work-id>, and spells out the RESOLVED (confirming, not building) and DEGRADED (declared before any source read) arms. RED observed first: 11 failures in tests/test_map_contract_wiring.py before the edit. m1's authored gate command runs the whole wiring file, so the template wiring and installer registration (m4/m5 substance) had to land here too -- recorded as a deviation.

verify-frame audited against deliverable 1 rather than trusted: all four refusal arms verified present and green (absent frame FRAME-MISSING exit 12, unknown anchor named, code-cut refused, no-receipt refused), frozen g1 exit vocabulary reused with codes 10 and 12 widened by documented reading only. c1 red was reconstructed against 6d35fe2, not observed in TDD order - recorded as a deviation. AUDIT GAP FOUND for a later slice: probe_fallbacks is dead code, never called by cmd_orient, and pin_substitutes writes no source label, so the receipt does not record which known fallback resolved; the degraded-arm frame fixtures DEGRADED_FRAME and UUNDECLARED_FALLBACK_FRAME are defined in tests but never used.

Wired the fallback oracle that attempt-1 left as dead code: cmd_orient now calls probe_fallbacks and records fallbacks_probed on every receipt (including RESOLVED ones, so the probe is not something an agent can suppress by claiming the map resolved), and pin_substitutes stamps each entry with source=known-fallback (in the fixed set AND present on disk) or agent-declared. Both labels asserted on receipts written by the real CLI, not on the pure helpers alone. The label is provenance only, never a discharge - an absent README.md is still agent-declared with content_hash null and still refuses. Also fixed a defect the self-test was pinning: the undeclared-fallback refusal renamed the offender to lowercase. Deliberately NOT claimed as closing the self-attestation gap; it converts half of it, since the agent still chooses what to declare.

Wiring audited against deliverable 2 rather than trusted, and it holds: verify-orientation is context c2 with no override_policy, verify-frame is plan c6 with the human-authority recorded-waiver policy, both use <repo-root>, and verify-frame is asserted ABSENT from context so the anti-vacuity property of m2's absent-frame refusal survives. Gate-vs-report stays a flag flip via --report-only, proven by CLI test not just by prose. The three template-pinning suites (context_manifest, context_declaration_lint, context_determinism) stay green because no context_refs entry was added. c1 red was reconstructed against 6d35fe2 - recorded as a deviation.

map_orient.py is registered on the commander bundle, the only bundle whose template invokes it, and the bundle-membership assertion is driven off the template rather than hardcoded so the two cannot drift apart. The companion question was answered by checking rather than by assuming: the module makes no dynamic sibling load and imports stdlib only, so it needs no SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS entry - stated explicitly in a code comment so the absence reads as a decision. c1 red reconstructed against 6d35fe2 - recorded as a deviation.

Mutation floor extended with three verify-frame mutations, the vacuous pass (an absent frame credited as a pass) being the one that matters, and all three are killed. Applied-before-red held on each: anchor unique = 1, gone after substitution = 0, replacement count delta exactly +1, evaluated BEFORE the floor was run, so a no-op mutation cannot be mistaken for a killed mutant. Required evidence green: 284 passed 419 subtests on the handoff command verbatim, 303 passed 433 subtests on the superset that also covers the new wiring file, self-test exit 0. IMPLEMENTER_RESULT written to .agent-work/issue-304/crew-handoffs/g2-result.md with all six deviations named, including the three red reconstructions and the one pre-existing self-test assertion I tightened.
